check: categorise every warning in the stress log, a class I had not separately audited
why: I had been counting ERROR, watchdog and OutOfMemory lines. Warnings were never enumerated as a class, so an unexpected warning could have been sitting in the 224 without my noticing - the same shape as an unexamined numeric claim.
everyWarnKind: 220 x Can't keep up! Is the server overloaded? Running Nms or N ticks behind - the profile's designed behaviour, since StressController documents that it deliberately overloads the server
1 x **** SERVER IS RUNNING IN OFFLINE/INSECURE MODE!
1 x The server will make no attempt to authenticate usernames. Beware.
1 x While this makes the game possible to play without internet access, it also opens up the ability for hackers to connect
1 x To change this, set online-mode to true in server.properties
verdict: Four distinct kinds, all accounted for. The 220 are the profile working as designed and the 4 are the standard offline-mode notice, which is expected for a local test server and is a property of server.properties rather than of the mod.
noUnexpectedWarning: Nothing in the warning class is unexplained, so there is no latent signal hiding among the volume.
theSingleErrorIsSeparate: The one ERROR is the mob-spawner fetch at 09:12:29 already recorded as benign: WallSpawnerGuard documents that the wall emits no real mob_spawner block entity, so the fetch failure is expected rather than a defect.
whatThisAddsToTheEvidence: Together with watchdogs 0, OutOfMemory 0 and the four distinct warning kinds, every log line produced in five and a half hours falls into a known category.
